summary: Front crawl breathing to the right: body rolled about 40 degrees, right arm recovering with a high elbow over the water, left arm extended forward under the surface, face turned sideways with the mouth in the bow-wave trough, flutter kick.

rules.why: high elbow: the recovering elbow clears the water
leading hand under the surface at the catch
mouth at the surface in the bow-wave trough to breathe

text.action: a swimmer swimming front crawl, taking a breath to the right
text.core: Lying prone at the surface, body rolled about 40 degrees onto the left side; right arm recovering over the water with the elbow high and bent, hand relaxed passing the shoulder near the water; left arm extended forward under the surface, palm down; head turned to the right with one goggle still in the water and the mouth open in the trough of the bow wave; legs long in a narrow flutter kick, toes pointed.
text.gaze: One eye above the water looking to the side.
cues: keep one goggle in the water when you breathe
high elbow, relaxed hand on the recovery
roll the body, not just the head
kinetic: bow wave curling around the head
white water and bubbles from the kick
water droplets streaming off the recovering arm
avoid: swimmer standing on the pool floor
body floating high out of the water
hair floating without a swim cap
head lifted forward out of the water
